ia_juego_en_076: Humans, living beings, come together. Beyond this planet lies an even bigger world… infinite, immense, full of mysteries, questions waiting for an answer and treasures waiting to be found.
ia_juego_en_077: In 1969, Neil Armstrong was the first person to reach the Moon.
ia_juego_en_078: What makes us human? What makes us who we really are? It isn’t our social skills, it isn’t our anatomy and, clearly, it isn’t our intelligence…
ia_juego_en_080: Yes, it’s the need to know what else is out there, to know what lies beyond what our eyes can see. It’s that thirst for knowledge, wanting to take the whole world and swallow it in a single bite, to know what moves the planet, every dimension, every particle, every wave and every electron.
ia_juego_en_081: Everything moves because we want to know more, do more, achieve more and reach higher… Not just looking at the sky and covering the sun with a finger; it’s standing before the sun and seeing, reflected in your eyes, those waves dancing so fiercely to the rhythm of the stars…
ia_juego_en_082: Time goes by and, the more time goes by, the more things emerge between Earth and space. All of this is the legacy of thousands of people, handed down from generation to generation, who dedicated their whole lives to finding answers.
ia_juego_en_083: Nothing is impossible, because when you try… it won’t always be what you expect, but you will always get a result…
ia_juego_en_084: Now it’s your turn… You carry the torch of wisdom, of knowledge, of curiosity and of perseverance… Show what you can do, push yourself and show how capable you are.
ia_juego_en_085: Because if you try, you can do it…

ia_juego_en_095: It all began in 2023, when four NASA volunteers lived for 378 days inside a simulated Mars base in Houston.
ia_juego_en_096: Since then, humanity has been getting ready to send people to Mars.
ia_juego_en_097: Today, in 2030, a small team is on its test mission at Mars Base One. It’s a simulation, but it’s very close to the real thing.

ia_juego_en_389: The base uses three resources: energy, oxygen, and shielding. Each one has three levels: low, medium, and high. If one hits zero, the base shuts down and the mission restarts.
ia_juego_en_390: Hello, Engineer Wenceslao! You know how every cable and every motor in the base works. There's never enough energy to power everything at once, so you decide which machines get power.
ia_juego_en_391: Ready to explore, Scientist Judith! Out there is a mysterious planet, dust storms, and incredible rocks. Your love of plants will keep the base alive.
ia_juego_en_392: Great to have you on board, Doctor Atlas! In space you have to take very good care of health and air. You'll make sure the whole crew is strong and ready for the adventure.
ia_juego_en_393: The battery can't power everything. Use the command console to choose where the energy goes today.
ia_juego_en_394: Notice: the signal to Earth is slow. Every message takes several minutes.
ia_juego_en_395: There's sunlight. Let's get to work! Clean the panels, change the filter, and water the plants before dark.
ia_juego_en_396: Notice: dust covered the solar panels and the battery isn't charging.
ia_juego_en_397: The Spirit and Opportunity robots had the same problem on Mars. Sometimes the wind cleaned them off, but you can't count on that.
ia_juego_en_398: There's dust on the panels again. There's no wind here to help us.
ia_juego_en_399: Great! The panels are shining again and the battery is rising. We'll have good light all night.
ia_juego_en_400: Air alert! The CO₂ filter is clogged and the spare doesn't fit in the slot.
ia_juego_en_401: In 1970, the Apollo 13 spacecraft had this same problem. The engineers invented an adapter out of plastic bags, cardboard, hoses, and tape.
ia_juego_en_402: The filter is saturated again. Time to build the adapter.
ia_juego_en_403: You did it! The filter is sealed tight and we're breathing fresh air. Great teamwork.
ia_juego_en_404: A little bad air got out. We're tired and the air is getting low.
ia_juego_en_405: Time to tend the garden! These plants help us have oxygen. In space, water floats in bubbles: give them only the drops they need.
ia_juego_en_406: In 2016, astronaut Scott Kelly tended the first zinnias to bloom on the Space Station. They got mold from the humidity, and he saved them.
ia_juego_en_407: The plants are thirsty, but watch out for too much water.
ia_juego_en_408: The cabin lights are dimming. Turn on your helmet flashlight to see the controls.
ia_juego_en_409: Notice: the shielding is weak. We should reinforce it tomorrow.
ia_juego_en_410: End of the first sol. It's very cold outside. On Mars, the night can drop below minus sixty degrees.
ia_juego_en_411: Teams on real missions have even lived on Mars time to work with their robots.
ia_juego_en_412: Mars is farther from the Sun than Earth. Less than half the light reaches here.
ia_juego_en_413: Good night. Saving energy in power-saving mode.
ia_juego_en_414: The Perseverance rover has microphones. It recorded the Martian wind, its own wheels, and even the Ingenuity helicopter.
ia_juego_en_415: The Mars sounds you're hearing are real NASA recordings. Good night.
ia_juego_en_416: The air on Mars is almost all carbon dioxide, CO₂. You can't breathe it.
ia_juego_en_417: Yes. It traveled with Perseverance and proved it can be done. In total it made 122 grams of oxygen, about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours.
ia_juego_en_419: An instrument on the Curiosity rover measures how much radiation reaches the Martian ground.
ia_juego_en_420: There's a dust storm in the sky. Some of them wrap around the whole planet.
ia_juego_en_422: Mars soil has salts called perchlorates. They're not good for plants, or to eat untreated.
ia_juego_en_423: Mars gravity is a little more than a third of Earth's. A 40-kilo astronaut would weigh about 15.
ia_juego_en_424: Good night. Recording a new jumping record.
ia_juego_en_425: News from the Sun. Scientists are watching the solar storms.
ia_juego_en_426: Services like NASA's DONKI and NOAA record these events.
ia_juego_en_428: Yes. In 2014, the Curiosity rover photographed it: it looked like a bright star, with the Moon beside it.
ia_juego_en_429: From 3 to 22 minutes, depending on where the planets are.
ia_juego_en_430: Alert! I detect a solar storm. It will arrive soon.
ia_juego_en_431: Notice: the shielding is taking more charge than normal.
ia_juego_en_432: In August 1972, the Sun unleashed a huge storm between two Moon missions. Nobody was in space; it was pure luck. That's why space weather is watched today.
ia_juego_en_433: Alert! A dust storm is covering the panels.
ia_juego_en_434: Reserves dropping. Calculating how long they'll last.
ia_juego_en_435: Alert! The CO₂ filter is saturated. The air is getting heavy.
ia_juego_en_436: Alert! Radiation outside has gone up.
ia_juego_en_438: Heat danger! A piece of the protective roof came loose and the cabin is heating up very fast.
ia_juego_en_439: Shade ready. The temperature is dropping.
ia_juego_en_440: The temperature is dropping. So is the energy.
ia_juego_en_441: In 1973, the Skylab station lost its sun shield during launch and heated up like an oven. Its first crew installed a sunshade and saved it.
ia_juego_en_442: Leak detected! The liquid that cools the solar panels is escaping into space.
ia_juego_en_444: In May 2013, the crew of the International Space Station saw white flakes of frozen coolant. Two astronauts went on a spacewalk and replaced the part that was failing.
ia_juego_en_445: Hull impact! Air is escaping through a crack. We have to close the hatch now.
ia_juego_en_446: Hatch sealed. The air was saved.
ia_juego_en_447: Hatch sealed. Some air was lost along the way.
ia_juego_en_448: In 1997, a cargo ship hit a module of the Russian space station Mir, with a NASA astronaut on board. The crew disconnected cables to seal the door, and the station kept working.
ia_juego_en_449: Alert! The greenhouse fan stopped and I don't know which part failed.
ia_juego_en_450: Notice: a message to Earth takes between 3 and 22 minutes to arrive. The reply takes just as long.
ia_juego_en_451: Message sent. Waiting for a reply. Oxygen is dropping in the meantime.
ia_juego_en_452: Restart underway. The batteries are working overtime.
ia_juego_en_453: A signal between Earth and Mars takes 3 to 22 minutes in each direction, depending on where the planets are. That's why a crew on Mars has to know how to decide on its own.
ia_juego_en_454: Ten whole sols have passed in this corner of the universe, and we're still here.
ia_juego_en_455: It wasn't just luck. It was curiosity, courage, and a will to learn.
ia_juego_en_456: Result: mission successful. Real data and good decisions.
ia_juego_en_457: Wenceslao, you are now a Junior Astronaut of Mars Base One.
ia_juego_en_458: Judith, you are now a Junior Astronaut of Mars Base One.
ia_juego_en_459: Atlas, you are now a Junior Astronaut of Mars Base One.
ia_juego_en_460: You learned that on Mars, teamwork and real information save the mission.
ia_juego_en_462: Energy depleted. The base shuts down and the mission restarts.
ia_juego_en_463: What we learned: on Mars, less than half the sunlight arrives. Dust covers the panels and storms make it worse.
ia_juego_en_464: When there isn't enough energy, you have to decide what stays on and save reserves before nightfall.
ia_juego_en_465: The Spirit and Opportunity robots lasted for years because the wind sometimes cleaned their panels. You can't wait for the wind: clean the panels in time.
ia_juego_en_466: Air with too much CO₂. The base shuts down and the mission restarts.
ia_juego_en_467: What we learned: on Mars the air is almost all CO₂. Filters and plants keep the air breathable.
ia_juego_en_468: Changing the filter in time is just as important as energy.
ia_juego_en_469: On Apollo 13, the air filled with CO₂ and the crew fixed it with tape, cardboard, and hoses. Check the filters and the plants carefully on your next try.
ia_juego_en_470: Shielding depleted. The base shuts down and the mission restarts.
ia_juego_en_471: What we learned: Mars has almost no natural protection against radiation. That's why the base needs shielding.
ia_juego_en_472: Following the space weather warnings gives us time to get ready.
ia_juego_en_473: In 1972, the Sun unleashed a huge storm right between two Moon missions. Today, space weather is watched so we can be ready.
